chunks: And Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated from his father, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Umayyah ibn Ali al-Qaisi, from Salim ibn Abi Hayya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When three names are gathered; Muhammad, Ali, and Hasan, then the fourth is the Qaim.

key_terms.أَسْمَاءٍ: Names, referring to the specific sequence of names in the Imams' lineage.
key_terms.الْحَسَنُ: Hasan, referring to Imam Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Qaim (The Riser), a title for the Awaited Imam, specifically referring to his rising to establish justice.
key_terms.مُحَمَّدٌ: Muhammad, referring to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) or Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him) depending on context, but here part of the sequence.

ai.seo_question: Who is the fourth name following Muhammad, Ali, and Hasan in the lineage of the Imams?
ai.summary: In *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to provide a specific linguistic and genealogical sign for the identity of the Awaited Imam. The sequence highlights the continuity of the Imamate through the four key figures of the Ahl al-Bayt, culminating in the Qaim, who is identified as Muhammad ibn al-Hasan. This hadith is frequently cited in Shia eschatological discourse to affirm the Mahdi's lineage and his role as the fourth in this specific prophetic-imamatic chain.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 201 - It is narrated from Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Ja’far Himyari from his father from Ahmad bin Hilal from Umayyah bin Ali Qaisi from Salim bin Abi Hayya from Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s) that he said:
“When three names, Muhammad, Ali, and Hasan come in consecution, their fourth is the Qaim (a.s).”
